calls.head: Top line on top line: O'Reilly vs. Thomas
calls.body: At home, the Predators keep sending O'Reilly’s line (Stamkos, O'Reilly and Bourque) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Andrew Brunette has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Blues’ first line is Holloway, Thomas and Snuggerud.
calls.call: The Predators’ L1 (Stamkos, O'Reilly and Bourque) spends at least 52% of its 5-on-5 time against the Blues’ first line, against about 40% with no line matching.
calls.nums: At home: 64% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 40% with no line matching

chips.tip: Nashville’s L1 (Stamkos, O'Reilly and Bourque) at home: 64% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ first lines. Matchups, Nashville home games this season, 10 games, 108 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.
With no line matching, this group would face first lines about 40% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

calls.happened: Nashville’s L1 (Stamkos, O'Reilly, Bourque) spent 67% of its 5-on-5 time against St. Louis’s L1 (9:51 of 14:41). The call needed 52%, halfway from the 40% it would get with no line matching to its home habit of 64%.

lane.tip: Share of this group’s 5-on-5 time against that line tonight (the filled dot). The ring is the call: halfway from what it would get with no line matching (the tick) to its home habit (the dotted mark), since part of any habit is luck. Reaching the ring holds the call; past the tick is partly; otherwise it didn’t happen.

calls.title: Brunette got his matchup
calls.plain: Nashville sent Stamkos, O'Reilly and Bourque out against the Blues’ first line for 67% of their 5-on-5 time, far more than the 40% they’d get with no line matching.
calls.said: Andrew Brunette would send Stamkos, O'Reilly and Bourque out against the Blues’ first line again

calls.head: Hofer gets another crack at the Predators
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Hofer has been shaky against the Predators, well below his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if he’s back to his usual self.
calls.call: If Hofer starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .912 than to his .865 against the Predators.
calls.nums: 7 starts against Nashville: .865 save percentage · .912 against everyone else

Hofer: .912 save percentage against everyone else since 2023-24, on 2,890 shots.

calls.happened: Joel Hofer stopped 26 of 28 shots (.929), against his usual .912 and his .866 against this team before tonight.

calls.title: The usual Hofer
calls.plain: Hofer played like his usual self, not like his record against the Predators. Just a coincidence, as we said.
calls.said: Hofer’s rough record against the Predators was a coincidence, and he’d look like himself

NSH.head: We had this close to even (51% for Nashville), and they came through.

STL.head: We had this close to even (49% for St. Louis), and it went Nashville’s way.

surprises.head: St. Louis couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: St. Louis usually gets some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Not tonight: a 4.4% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 6.9% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 50 games.

story.head: The Predators get past the Blues
paras: Jimmy Snuggerud got the scoring started for the Blues on the power play midway through the first. Steven Stamkos made it 1-1 for Nashville on the power play three minutes later, and Ross Colton put the Predators ahead for good midway through the second. Nick Perbix sealed it into the empty net with a minute and a half left.

The Predators had a bit more of the good stuff. Juuse Saros made 25 saves for the Preds, and Joel Hofer stopped 26 of 28 at the other end. The Predators moved to 8-4-5 and climbed to fourth in the Central, while the Blues fell to 7-8-2, sixth in the Central.

items.text: Four straight wins for the Predators.
The Blues are winless in three (0-2-1).
Ross Colton has scored in three straight games.
The Predators have won both meetings this season.
